{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01YLqhZ9JXXnAaDMx2dp8eAU","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Physicians EMR, LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-16\n     4→Developer website: https://www.ipclinical.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Physicians EMR, LLC is a small, privately held health IT company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Longwood, Florida (Orlando metro area). The company was founded by Dr. Wasim Ahmar, a practicing cardiologist who also runs Heart Experts of Florida from the same office address (450 W. SR-434, Suite 3010, Longwood, FL 32750). LinkedIn lists the company as having 51-200 employees. The company's stated vision is to become \"the market-leading provider of technology-enabled solutions addressing business challenges for medical practices.\"\n     9→\n    10→IPClinical combines a cloud-based EHR/practice management software platform with outsourced services (billing, transcription, credentialing, scheduling, documentation, and \"e-scribe\" virtual scribe services). The company appears to target small-to-mid-size ambulatory practices. Testimonials on their website reference cardiology, spine care, primary care, and diagnostic centers, with client relationships spanning 6-8 years. The company has minimal public visibility — no reviews were found on G2, Capterra, or KLAS, and LinkedIn shows only ~300 followers. This is a very small vendor with a niche market presence.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: IPClinical\n    13→\n    14→CHPL ID: 10278\n    15→CHPL Product Number: 15.05.05.2163.PEMR.01.00.1.200123\n    16→Version: 2.1\n    17→Certification Date: 2020-01-23\n    18→\n    19→### What It Is\n    20→\n    21→IPClinical is a cloud-based Electronic Health Records (EHR) and practice management platform with integrated revenue cycle management. The certified module appears to be the full product — the company does not appear to have separate product lines. The system is described as \"easy to use as a smart phone\" and \"built on latest technology.\" It is broadly certified across 47 ONC criteria, spanning clinical documentation (a)(1)-(a)(15), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(2), patient portal (e)(1)-(e)(3), clinical quality measures (c)(1)-(c)(4), public health reporting (f)(1)-(f)(2), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10)). The interoperability engine used is \"EMR Direct Interoperability Engine 2017\" (per the mandatory disclosures page).\n    22→\n    23→### Users & Market\n    24→\n    25→IPClinical targets ambulatory medical practices, apparently across multiple specialties. The vendor's testimonials reference cardiology, spine care, primary care, and diagnostic centers. Given the founder is a cardiologist, cardiology appears to be a core market. The company is based in Central Florida and serves \"hundreds of healthcare providers\" per their website claims, though this is unverifiable. No notable large health system deployments were identified. There are no third-party reviews on major platforms (G2, Capterra, KLAS), suggesting very limited market penetration. The product is not featured on any industry \"top EHR\" lists.\n    26→\n    27→### Modules & Functionality\n    28→\n    29→Based on the vendor's website and service pages, IPClinical includes the following modules and capabilities:\n    30→\n    31→**EHR / Clinical:**\n    32→- Electronic order entry (CPOE) for inpatient and outpatient settings (vendor website)\n    33→- E-prescribing integrated with \"America's renowned medication database\" — likely First Databank or similar (EHR page)\n    34→- Patient chart management and health records storage (EHR page)\n    35→- Clinical documentation — the vendor also offers an \"E-Scribe\" virtual scribe service that handles documentation of patient visits, including patient history, physical examination findings, procedure documentation, clinical notes, and assessment/plans (E-Scribe page)\n    36→- Document management for capturing, tracking, and storing PDFs, Word files, and digital images (EHR page)\n    37→- Task management system with electronic tracking, alerts, and task assignment (EHR page)\n    38→- Clinical quality measure tracking — supports 12 CQMs including diabetes, hypertension, and preventive care (mandatory disclosures page)\n    39→- Immunization reporting to public health agencies (mandatory disclosures page)\n    40→\n    41→**Patient Engagement:**\n    42→- Patient portal for viewing, downloading, and transmitting clinical information (EHR page)\n    43→- Online patient registration (medical documentation page)\n    44→\n    45→**Scheduling:**\n    46→- Appointment scheduling with provider availability matching (scheduling page)\n    47→- Appointment reminders (proactive day-before confirmation calls) (scheduling page)\n    48→- Cancellation list management (scheduling page)\n    49→- Test scheduling (scheduling page)\n    50→- Call routing management (scheduling page)\n    51→\n    52→**Revenue Cycle Management / Billing:**\n    53→- In-app insurance eligibility verification (EHR page)\n    54→- Charge capture with procedure codes, modifiers, and patient demographics (billing page)\n    55→- Medical coding by certified coders (billing page)\n    56→- Claim submission to insurance within 24 hours (billing page)\n    57→- Rejection/denial management and resubmission (billing page)\n    58→- Payment posting and reconciliation (billing page)\n    59→- Accounts receivable management (billing page)\n    60→- Authorization services for insurance pre-approvals (services page)\n    61→\n    62→**Medical Documentation & Records:**\n    63→- Medical transcription of dictated notes (documentation page)\n    64→- Medical record retrieval from hospitals, clinics, and other providers (documentation page)\n    65→- Release of Information (ROI) form processing (documentation page)\n    66→- Fax management — incoming and outgoing (documentation page)\n    67→- Worksheet and handwritten transcription conversion (documentation page)\n    68→\n    69→**Other Services (outsourced, not necessarily in the software):**\n    70→- Provider credentialing (services page)\n    71→- Remote patient monitoring with digital devices — weight scales, blood pressure monitors (documentation page)\n    72→- Cardiac device home monitoring (documentation page)\n    73→- Digital marketing for practices (services page)\n    74→- Medical assistance / virtual assistant for bookkeeping (services page)\n    75→\n    76→**Notable:** The medical documentation page mentions \"leveraging EpicCare electronic health records to access medical templates, patient history, and referral information.\" This is an unusual reference — it may indicate the E-Scribe service also works with Epic-based facilities (e.g., hospital ED documentation), or it could be residual/inaccurate website content. It's unclear whether this is part of the IPClinical product itself or a separate service offering.\n    77→\n    78→### Data & Content\n    79→\n    80→Based on the described features, IPClinical stores and manages the following types of data:\n    81→\n    82→- **Patient demographics and registration data** — implied by scheduling, billing, and EHR features\n    83→- **Clinical notes and encounter documentation** — explicitly described across EHR and E-Scribe services\n    84→- **Medical history** — explicitly mentioned on EHR feature page\n    85→- **Medications and prescriptions** — e-prescribing is a core feature\n    86→- **Test results (lab and imaging)** — EHR page mentions \"test results\" and mandatory disclosures mention \"lab and imaging results through configurable interfaces\"\n    87→- **Treatment plans** — explicitly mentioned on EHR feature page\n    88→- **Orders (CPOE)** — electronic order entry is a core feature\n    89→- **Problems/conditions** — implied by clinical documentation and CQM tracking\n    90→- **Allergies** — implied by (a)(8) certification criterion\n    91→- **Immunizations** — public health immunization reporting is certified\n    92→- **Vitals** — implied by (a)(6) certification criterion\n    93→- **Clinical quality measure data** — 12 CQMs tracked per mandatory disclosures\n    94→- **Insurance/eligibility information** — in-app eligibility verification described\n    95→- **Claims and billing data** — comprehensive RCM features described\n    96→- **Payment and accounts receivable data** — payment posting and AR management described\n    97→- **Appointment/scheduling data** — scheduling module described\n    98→- **Tasks and alerts** — task management system described\n    99→- **Documents (PDFs, images, scanned records)** — document management described\n   100→- **Patient portal messages/communications** — patient portal described, though messaging specifics are thin\n   101→- **Faxes** — fax management described\n   102→- **Remote patient monitoring data** — cardiac monitoring and RPM with digital devices mentioned on documentation page\n   103→\n   104→**Gaps and uncertainties:**\n   105→- The vendor website does not clearly distinguish between features in the software product vs. outsourced services. For example, medical transcription and credentialing may be human services performed using the platform rather than software features per se.\n   106→- No detailed data model or database schema information is available.\n   107→- The website doesn't specifically mention referrals management, care plans (as a structured feature), or clinical decision support, though some of these are implied by the broad certification criteria ((a)(9) for CDS, (a)(13) for referrals).\n   108→- No information was found about imaging/PACS integration beyond \"configurable interfaces.\"\n   109→- The distinction between what the E-Scribe service documents vs. what the EHR software itself captures is unclear.\n   110→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. The company was founded by Dr. Wasim Ahmar, a practicing cardiologist who also runs Heart Experts of Florida from the same office address (450 W. SR-434, Suite 3010, Longwood, FL 32750). LinkedIn lists the company as having 51-200 employees. The company's stated vision is to become \"the market-leading provider of technology-enabled solutions addressing business challenges for medical practices.\"\n\nIPClinical combines a cloud-based EHR/practice management software platform with outsourced services (billing, transcription, credentialing, scheduling, documentation, and \"e-scribe\" virtual scribe services). The company appears to target small-to-mid-size ambulatory practices. Testimonials on their website reference cardiology, spine care, primary care, and diagnostic centers, with client relationships spanning 6-8 years. The company has minimal public visibility — no reviews were found on G2, Capterra, or KLAS, and LinkedIn shows only ~300 followers. This is a very small vendor with a niche market presence.\n\n## Product: IPClinical\n\nCHPL ID: 10278\nCHPL Product Number: 15.05.05.2163.PEMR.01.00.1.200123\nVersion: 2.1\nCertification Date: 2020-01-23\n\n### What It Is\n\nIPClinical is a cloud-based Electronic Health Records (EHR) and practice management platform with integrated revenue cycle management. The certified module appears to be the full product — the company does not appear to have separate product lines. The system is described as \"easy to use as a smart phone\" and \"built on latest technology.\" It is broadly certified across 47 ONC criteria, spanning clinical documentation (a)(1)-(a)(15), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(2), patient portal (e)(1)-(e)(3), clinical quality measures (c)(1)-(c)(4), public health reporting (f)(1)-(f)(2), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10)). The interoperability engine used is \"EMR Direct Interoperability Engine 2017\" (per the mandatory disclosures page).\n\n### Users & Market\n\nIPClinical targets ambulatory medical practices, apparently across multiple specialties. The vendor's testimonials reference cardiology, spine care, primary care, and diagnostic centers. Given the founder is a cardiologist, cardiology appears to be a core market. The company is based in Central Florida and serves \"hundreds of healthcare providers\" per their website claims, though this is unverifiable. No notable large health system deployments were identified. There are no third-party reviews on major platforms (G2, Capterra, KLAS), suggesting very limited market penetration. The product is not featured on any industry \"top EHR\" lists.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on the vendor's website and service pages, IPClinical includes the following modules and capabilities:\n\n**EHR / Clinical:**\n- Electronic order entry (CPOE) for inpatient and outpatient settings (vendor website)\n- E-prescribing integrated with \"America's renowned medication database\" — likely First Databank or similar (EHR page)\n- Patient chart management and health records storage (EHR page)\n- Clinical documentation — the vendor also offers an \"E-Scribe\" virtual scribe service that handles documentation of patient visits, including patient history, physical examination findings, procedure documentation, clinical notes, and assessment/plans (E-Scribe page)\n- Document management for capturing, tracking, and storing PDFs, Word files, and digital images (EHR page)\n- Task management system with electronic tracking, alerts, and task assignment (EHR page)\n- Clinical quality measure tracking — supports 12 CQMs including diabetes, hypertension, and preventive care (mandatory disclosures page)\n- Immunization reporting to public health agencies (mandatory disclosures page)\n\n**Patient Engagement:**\n- Patient portal for viewing, downloading, and transmitting clinical information (EHR page)\n- Online patient registration (medical documentation page)\n\n**Scheduling:**\n- Appointment scheduling with provider availability matching (scheduling page)\n- Appointment reminders (proactive day-before confirmation calls) (scheduling page)\n- Cancellation list management (scheduling page)\n- Test scheduling (scheduling page)\n- Call routing management (scheduling page)\n\n**Revenue Cycle Management / Billing:**\n- In-app insurance eligibility verification (EHR page)\n- Charge capture with procedure codes, modifiers, and patient demographics (billing page)\n- Medical coding by certified coders (billing page)\n- Claim submission to insurance within 24 hours (billing page)\n- Rejection/denial management and resubmission (billing page)\n- Payment posting and reconciliation (billing page)\n- Accounts receivable management (billing page)\n- Authorization services for insurance pre-approvals (services page)\n\n**Medical Documentation & Records:**\n- Medical transcription of dictated notes (documentation page)\n- Medical record retrieval from hospitals, clinics, and other providers (documentation page)\n- Release of Information (ROI) form processing (documentation page)\n- Fax management — incoming and outgoing (documentation page)\n- Worksheet and handwritten transcription conversion (documentation page)\n\n**Other Services (outsourced, not necessarily in the software):**\n- Provider credentialing (services page)\n- Remote patient monitoring with digital devices — weight scales, blood pressure monitors (documentation page)\n- Cardiac device home monitoring (documentation page)\n- Digital marketing for practices (services page)\n- Medical assistance / virtual assistant for bookkeeping (services page)\n\n**Notable:** The medical documentation page mentions \"leveraging EpicCare electronic health records to access medical templates, patient history, and referral information.\" This is an unusual reference — it may indicate the E-Scribe service also works with Epic-based facilities (e.g., hospital ED documentation), or it could be residual/inaccurate website content. It's unclear whether this is part of the IPClinical product itself or a separate service offering.\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the described features, IPClinical stores and manages the following types of data:\n\n- **Patient demographics and registration data** — implied by scheduling, billing, and EHR features\n- **Clinical notes and encounter documentation** — explicitly described across EHR and E-Scribe services\n- **Medical history** — explicitly mentioned on EHR feature page\n- **Medications and prescriptions** — e-prescribing is a core feature\n- **Test results (lab and imaging)** — EHR page mentions \"test results\" and mandatory disclosures mention \"lab and imaging results through configurable interfaces\"\n- **Treatment plans** — explicitly mentioned on EHR feature page\n- **Orders (CPOE)** — electronic order entry is a core feature\n- **Problems/conditions** — implied by clinical documentation and CQM tracking\n- **Allergies** — implied by (a)(8) certification criterion\n- **Immunizations** — public health immunization reporting is certified\n- **Vitals** — implied by (a)(6) certification criterion\n- **Clinical quality measure data** — 12 CQMs tracked per mandatory disclosures\n- **Insurance/eligibility information** — in-app eligibility verification described\n- **Claims and billing data** — comprehensive RCM features described\n- **Payment and accounts receivable data** — payment posting and AR management described\n- **Appointment/scheduling data** — scheduling module described\n- **Tasks and alerts** — task management system described\n- **Documents (PDFs, images, scanned records)** — document management described\n- **Patient portal messages/communications** — patient portal described, though messaging specifics are thin\n- **Faxes** — fax management described\n- **Remote patient monitoring data** — cardiac monitoring and RPM with digital devices mentioned on documentation page\n\n**Gaps and uncertainties:**\n- The vendor website does not clearly distinguish between features in the software product vs. outsourced services. For example, medical transcription and credentialing may be human services performed using the platform rather than software features per se.\n- No detailed data model or database schema information is available.\n- The website doesn't specifically mention referrals management, care plans (as a structured feature), or clinical decision support, though some of these are implied by the broad certification criteria ((a)(9) for CDS, (a)(13) for referrals).\n- No information was found about imaging/PACS integration beyond \"configurable interfaces.\"\n- The distinction between what the E-Scribe service documents vs. what the EHR software itself captures is unclear.\n","numLines":110,"startLine":1,"totalLines":110}}}

All Right Reserved. No reproduction or redistribution without written permission\n\nP a g e |1\n\n\f§ 170.315 (b)(10) Electronic Health Information export\n\nProduct Name and Version\nName: IPClinical\nVersion: 2.1\n\n§170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export\nThe application provides export of Electronic Health Information (EHI) for a single patient as well as for\npatient population in the following formats:\n1. C-CDA: IPClinical is capable to export both single patient and patient population EHI through CCDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) including the data classes expressed in\nstandard §170.213 United States Core Data for Interoperability (USCDI), Version 1.\nIn order to understand how to process the EHI after export, kindly refer to the following C-CDA\nspecifications provided on HL7 website:\no\n\n§170.205(a)(3) Health Level 7 (HL7) Implementation Guide for CDA Release 2: IHE Health\nStory Consolidation, DSTU Release 1.1 (US Realm) Draft Standard for Trial Use July 2012\n\no\n\n§170.205(a)(4) HL7® Implementation Guide for CDA® Release 2: Consolidated CDA\nTemplates for Clinical Notes (US Realm), Draft Standard for Trial Use Release 2.1 August\n2015, June 2019 (with Errata)\n\no\n\n§170.205(a)(5) HL7® CDA R2 IG: C-CDA Templates for Clinical Notes R2.1 Companion\nGuide, Release 2, October 2019, IBR approved for § 170.205(a)(5)\n\n2. FHIR: IPClinical also supports following standards of FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability\nResources) for single patient and patient population EHI export:\no §170.215(a)(2) FHIR® US Core Implementation Guide STU V3.1.1\no §170.215(a)(4) HL7® FHIR® Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR®) (V1.0.1:STU 1)\nKindly refer to IPClinical – (g)(10) FHIR API Documentation for API specifications.\n3. Excel/PDF: EHI including patient clinical information is exported in above-mentioned formats.\nEHI including other information such as Patient Documents, Scheduling & Appointments and\nBilling & Financial information can be exported via Excel/PDF file formats. All patient documents\nincluding lab results, radiology reports and any other scanned/imported/ faxed documents can\nbe exported in PDF format. Images available under Imaging Result Reports are exported through\nFHIR format as well. In regards to scheduling and appointments, IPClinical is capable to export\nthat information via both Excel and PDF formats. Lastly, most of the billing and financial\ninformation can be exported in Excel format and some of it can also be exported in PDF format.\n\nVersion 2.1\n© 2023 IPClinical. All Right Reserved. No reproduction or redistribution without written permission\n\nP a g e |2","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"40d60e77-9bb7-49f3-8788-de9bac2a89bb","uuid":"85216170-c733-4fdd-b320-a4da9ad5004b","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"§ 170.315 (b)(10) Electronic Health Information export\n\nIPClinical v2.1\n\n§ 170.315 (b)(10) Electronic Health Information export\nAuthor\nCreation Date\n\nIPClinical\nNovember 15th, 2023\n\nVersion 2.1\n© 2023 IPClinical. No reproduction or redistribution without written permission\n\nP a g e |3\n\n\fIPClinical (g)(10) API Documentation\n\nIntroduction\nIn this documentation we will list all the steps required to access Protected Health Information (PHI)\nbased on the documentation of an open API. The API makes health information broadly available using\nFHIR®, a set of clinical interoperability resources under the umbrella of the HL7 standards organization.\nFHIR is based on common web standards that can be reached through a RESTful protocol in which each\nFHIR resource has a known URL.\n\nFHIR Server Endpoint\nFHIR: https://staging.pemr.com:93/api\nAuthentication Server: https://staging.pemr.com:93/api/authorize/authorize\n\nTypes of SMART-On-FHIR applications supported\nStandalone App: SMART on FHIR confidential client with a patient context, refresh token, and OpenID\nConnect (OIDC) identity token.\nEHR Embedded app: Demonstrate the ability to perform an EHR launch to a SMART on FHIR.\nSmart Backend Services App (Multi-patient authorization and API): These are server-to-server backend\napplications e.g., Export clinical data for multiple patients in a group. This app is system level app without\nany UI.\n\nTypes of Supported Authentications\nSymmetric (“client secret”) authentication (HL7.FHIR.UV.SMART-APP-LAUNCH\\Example App Launch for\nSymmetric Client Auth - FHIR v3.1.1)\nAsymmetric (“private key JWT”) authentication (HL7.FHIR.UV.SMART-APP-LAUNCH\\Example App Launch\nfor Asymmetric Client Auth – FHIR v3.1.1)\nPublic Clients (HL7.FHIR.UV.SMART-APP-LAUNCH\\Example App Launch for Public Client - FHIR v3.1.1)\n\nSteps for Smart App Launch\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n\nClient App Registration\nRetrieve. well-known/smart-configuration\nObtain authorization code\nObtain access token\nAccess FHIR API\nRefresh Token to obtain new access token\n\nVersion 2.1\n© 2023 IPClinical. All Right Reserved. No reproduction or redistribution without written permission\n\nP a g e |4\n\n\fIPClinical (g)(10) API Documentation\n\nInteroperability requirements with IPClinical for Native Applications\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n\nNative applications MUST be capable of storing the refresh token in a secure manner similar to the\nrequirements of storing a secret for confidential apps.\nNative applications must request the offline_scope in their initial API request in order to receive a\nrefresh token\nNative application refresh tokens are valid for 3 months before they must be renewed.\nNative applications can only communicate with IPClinical over a TLS secured channel in order to\nensure the safe transmission of the refresh token.\nNative applications must use the Authorization Code grant flow in order to receive a refresh token.\n\nClient APP Registration\nBefore a SMART app can run against an EHR, the app must be registered with that EHR’s authorization\nservice. We are using JWT Client Request process. Third-party applications must contact with the following\ninfo to register their apps:\n• The app name\n• The necessary APIs / Scopes\n• Any redirect URIs\n• Launch_URL (optional)\n• URL to JWK Set (Only for apps supporting asymmetric client authentication)\nThe application is created by the EHR admin after confirming the app’s registration parameters and\ncommunicates a client_id to the app. FHIR APIs (of any supported version) listed within the USCDI v1 core\ndata set will support only reads data from FHIR server.\nRetrieve. well-known/smart-configuration:\nIn order to obtain launch context and request authorization to access FHIR resources, the app\ndiscovers the EHR FHIR server’s SMART configuration metadata, including OAuth {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01Nf8bsoNxyK8MsYUXU6m3gd","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01FL6nAN8diakqx5hQuXD8d8","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/physicians-emr-llc--ipclinical/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Physicians EMR, LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-16\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://ipclinical.com/documentation/b_10_Electronic_Health_Information_export.pdf\n- CHPL IDs: 10278\n- Product: IPClinical v2.1\n- Certification Date: 2020-01-23\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — HTTP HEAD request to the registered URL returned HTTP 200\n   with `Content-Type: application/pdf` and `Content-Length: 466885` (about 467KB).\n   Direct file download, no redirects.\n\n   ```bash\n   curl -sI -L \"https://ipclinical.com/documentation/b_10_Electronic_Health_Information_export.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n\n2. **Downloaded the PDF** directly:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://ipclinical.com/documentation/b_10_Electronic_Health_Information_export.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o b_10_Electronic_Health_Information_export.pdf\n   ```\n   Verified: `file` confirms \"PDF document, version 1.5, 2 page(s)\". Created November 23, 2023 by Ahmed Tariq using Microsoft Word 2016.\n\n3. **Extracted hyperlinks from the PDF**. Found:\n   - Links to external standards (HL7, HealthIT) — not followed per instructions\n   - Link to `https://ipclinical.com/mu-disclousure` (mandatory disclosures page), referenced as the location of \"(g)(10) FHIR API Documentation\"\n   - No embedded files or attachments in the PDF\n\n4. **Checked the mandatory disclosures page** (`https://ipclinical.com/mu-disclousure`).\n   Found two additional API documentation PDFs linked:\n   - `https://ipclinical.com/documentation/IPClinical_g10_API_Documentation.pdf`\n   - `https://ipclinical.com/documentation/IPClinical-api-documentation.pdf`\n\n   Downloaded both since the (b)(10) PDF explicitly says \"Kindly refer to IPClinical – (g)(10) FHIR API Documentation for API specifications\" when describing the FHIR export format.\n\n5. **Also checked** the `/documentation/` directory — returns 403 Forbidden after redirecting to `www.ipclinical.com/documentation/`.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire (b)(10) EHI export documentation is a **single 2-page PDF**. Page 1 is a cover page with the IPClinical logo; page 2 is the actual content. The document describes three export formats:\n\n### Format 1: C-CDA\n- Supports both single patient and patient population export\n- Includes USCDI Version 1 data classes\n- References three C-CDA specifications: HL7 CDA R2 IHE Health Story Consolidation DSTU 1.1 (2012), HL7 C-CDA R2.1 (2015/2019), and the C-CDA R2.1 Companion Guide R2 (2019)\n- No data dictionary, no field mapping, no examples — just a statement that C-CDA is supported\n\n### Format 2: FHIR\n- Supports single patient and patient population export\n- References FHIR US Core IG STU V3.1.1 and FHIR Bulk Data Access V1.0.1 STU 1\n- Points to the separate g(10) FHIR API Documentation (121-page PDF) for API specifications\n- The g(10) documentation covers these US Core FHIR resources:\n  - Patient, AllergyIntolerance, CarePlan, CareTeam, Condition, Device (Implantable), DiagnosticReport (notes & labs), DocumentReference, Encounter, Goal, Immunization, MedicationRequest, Observation (vitals, smoking status, lab results, pediatric measures), Procedure, Organization, Practitioner, Provenance\n  - Includes SMART on FHIR authentication, Bulk Data export endpoints, and a full CapabilityStatement\n- There is also an older, simpler API doc (8 pages, \"IPClinical API v5.0\") that describes a proprietary API returning C-CDA XML\n\n### Format 3: Excel/PDF\n- Patient Documents: lab results, radiology reports, scanned/imported/faxed documents exported as PDF\n- Scheduling & Appointments: exportable in both Excel and PDF\n- Billing & Financial information: \"most\" exportable in Excel, \"some\" also in PDF\n- Imaging Result Reports: exported through FHIR format as well\n- **No data dictionary or schema for the Excel exports** — no description of columns, data types, or structure\n- **No sample files or examples**\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nIPClinical's (b)(10) documentation describes a multi-format export strategy that attempts to cover data beyond the USCDI/US Core subset. This is a positive sign — the vendor recognizes that (b)(10) requires more than just FHIR US Core data. However, the documentation is extremely thin on specifics.\n\n**Clearly covered (via C-CDA/FHIR):**\n- Demographics / patient information\n- Allergies\n- Conditions / problem lists\n- Medications / prescriptions\n- Lab results\n- Vital signs\n- Immunizations\n- Procedures\n- Clinical notes (via DocumentReference)\n- Encounters\n- Care plans / goals\n- Care team information\n- Implantable devices\n- Smoking status\n\n**Mentioned but poorly documented (via Excel/PDF):**\n- Billing & financial information — described as \"most\" exportable in Excel, but no data dictionary, no column definitions, no description of what \"most\" means or what's excluded\n- Scheduling & appointments — exportable in Excel/PDF, but no schema\n- Patient documents — PDFs of lab results, radiology, scanned/faxed docs\n\n**Likely missing or not mentioned:**\n- Insurance/eligibility data — the product stores this (per product research) but the export documentation doesn't specifically mention it beyond \"billing & financial\"\n- Claims data and charge capture details — subsumed under \"billing\" but undefined\n- Accounts receivable / payment data — not specifically mentioned\n- Task/alert data — the product has a task management system, not mentioned in export\n- Patient portal communications — the product has a patient portal, no export mentioned\n- Remote patient monitoring data — the product supports RPM and cardiac device monitoring, not mentioned in export\n- Fax records — the product manages faxes, not mentioned as exportable data (though \"faxed documents\" as PDFs are)\n- E-Scribe/virtual scribe data — unclear if this generates structured data beyond clinical notes\n\nThe fundamental problem is that the Excel/PDF exports are described in a single paragraph with no specifics. A developer receiving an Excel file of \"billing & financial information\" would have no way to know what fields are included, what the columns mean, or how to map them to other systems.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a reasonable combination of formats:\n- **C-CDA** for structured clinical data (USCDI v1 scope)\n- **FHIR US Core 3.1.1 + Bulk Data** for the same clinical data via API\n- **Excel/PDF** for non-clinical data (billing, scheduling, documents)\n\nThe C-CDA and FHIR formats are well-documented in their respective spec documents (121-page g(10) API doc). The Excel/PDF formats have **zero documentation** — no schema, no column definitions, no examples.\n\nThis is a classic (b)(10) pattern: the vendor has invested heavily in their g(10) FHIR API (which is genuinely detailed) and then bolted on a vague mention of Excel/PDF export for everything else. The result is that a third party could reconstruct the USCDI clinical data from the FHIR/C-CDA export, but would be flying blind on the billing, scheduling, and document exports.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n- **FHIR/C-CDA documentation**: Good. The 121-page g(10) API doc includes resource-level documentation with field descriptions, search parameters, examples, and a full CapabilityStatement. This is a real, working API specification.\n- **(b)(10) documentation**: Very poor. A 2-page document that reads like a compliance checkbox. No data dictionary, no worked examples, no sample files, no export instructions, no screenshots of the export interface. The document says what formats exist but not what's in them.\n- **Excel/PDF exports**: Undocumented. A receiving party would have to inspect the actual export files to understand their structure.\n\nA developer could implement a FHIR US Core import based on the g(10) docs. A developer could **not** implement an import of the billing/scheduling Excel exports based solely on this documentation — there is nothing to implement against.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Clinical data (FHIR)**: Field-level documentation exists in the g(10) doc. FHIR resources have defined schemas, search parameters, and value sets. The CapabilityStatement lists supported interactions.\n- **Clinical data (C-CDA)**: Relies entirely on external C-CDA specifications. No vendor-specific mapping or customization documented.\n- **Non-clinical data (Excel/PDF)**: No field-level documentation at all. No data types, no value sets, no relationships between tables, no cardinality.\n- **No versioning or change history** beyond the document version (2.1) and creation date (Nov 2023).\n\nThe documentation presents a two-tier system: the FHIR/g(10) layer is professional and detailed, while the (b)(10)-specific layer (the parts that go beyond USCDI) is a single paragraph of prose with no technical substance.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://ipclinical.com/documentation/b_10_Electronic_Health_Information_export.pdf\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The `/documentation/` directory listing is forbidden (403), so there's no way to discover additional documentation files beyond what's linked from known pages.\n- No additional EHI-specific documentation was found beyond the single 2-page PDF and the referenced g(10) API docs.\n- No data dictionary, schema, or sample export files exist at the registered URL or on the mandatory disclosures page.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":435,"cache_read_input_tokens":56352,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":435},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"40d60e77-9bb7-49f3-8788-de9bac2a89bb","uuid":"bce5192f-42ae-4614-9223-468baad59f43"}
